headline: Monongahela Forest Entry and Discovery Center Access
reservation: While there is no general entry fee or reservation system for the Seneca Rocks Discovery Center or the main hiking trails, nearby campgrounds such as Seneca Shadows often require booking through Recreation.gov during peak foliage. Technical climbing is permitted but may be subject to seasonal closures for raptor nesting. Always verify the current status of facilities on the Forest Service site.

days.title: The Vertical Fins of Seneca
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Mouth of Seneca

stops.name: Seneca Rocks Trail
stops.detail: Hike the 1.3-mile steady incline to the observation platform for a high-angle view of the North Fork valley.

stops.name: Seneca Rocks Discovery Center
stops.detail: Learn about the geological formation of the Tuscarora quartzite fins and the region's cultural history at this educational hub.

days.driving: Walking from local parking areas; allow 2–3 hours for the hike
days.note: The final scramble beyond the observation deck is not maintained and contains sheer drops.

days.title: Potomac Highlands Heights

stops.name: Spruce Knob
stops.detail: Drive to the highest point in West Virginia to walk the Whispering Spruce Trail among wind-swept trees.

stops.name: North Fork South Branch Potomac River
stops.detail: Relax by the riverbanks near the base of the rocks, a popular area for trout fishing and wading.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the mountain roads to Spruce Knob; conditions vary with weather
days.note: Spruce Knob is significantly cooler than the valley; bring an extra layer even in summer.

days.title: Underground and Scenic Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Mouth of Seneca

stops.name: Smoke Hole Caverns
stops.detail: Take a guided tour through these local caverns to see unique stalactite formations.

stops.name: Smoke Hole Canyon
stops.detail: Drive through this rugged gorge, known for its sheer limestone cliffs and remote forest scenery.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 2.5 hours; mountain roads are winding and require caution
days.note: Cavern tours operate on specific schedules; check availability locally or via their official portal.

intel.title: Discovery Center Capacity
intel.text: The main parking lot at the Discovery Center fills rapidly on weekends in October. Arrive before 9 AM or prepare to use designated overflow areas farther from the trailhead.

intel.title: National Radio Quiet Zone
intel.text: Cellular service is extremely limited or non-existent in this region due to the National Radio Quiet Zone. Rely on paper maps and inform others of your itinerary before entering the forest.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: Mouth of Seneca has very limited services; fill your tank in larger gateway towns like Petersburg or Elkins. Do not expect to find fuel or groceries within the National Forest boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: High-altitude roads leading to Spruce Knob may be closed by snow from late autumn through spring. Check the Monongahela National Forest road status page before planning mountain ascents.

intel.title: Climbing Restrictions
intel.text: Specific cliff faces may be closed seasonally to protect nesting Peregrine Falcons. Check the bulletin boards at the Discovery Center for the latest raptor protection zones.

plan.arrival: After the two-hour drive from Shenandoah Valley Regional Airport, check in to your mountain lodge or camp and pick up topographic maps at the Discovery Center.
plan.vehicle: A vehicle with good brakes and tires is essential for the steep, winding mountain passes; RVs should verify length restrictions for Smoke Hole Canyon.
plan.goldenHour: The observation platform at the top of the rocks offers a westward view of the valley, though fog often settles in the river valley at dawn.
